scenes.label: Meet Tara
scenes.title: One password, three doors
scenes.caption: Meet Tara. She's growing a floating island garden in her favourite game, Sky Garden. She also uses a school portal for homework, and an email account for class news. To keep things easy, she uses the same password for all three. One key, opening three doors.
scenes.dialogue: My sky garden is almost finished!

scenes.label: The breach
scenes.title: The game got hacked.
scenes.caption: One morning, a message arrives from Sky Garden. The game's website was hacked, and passwords were stolen. This is called a data breach, and it wasn't Tara's fault. But then more alerts pop up. Someone signed in to her school portal. Then her email. Her accounts fall like dominoes.
scenes.dialogue: My school portal too? And my email?

scenes.label: Why it spread
scenes.title: How did it spread?
scenes.caption: Tara tells Mum right away. Mum explains that someone tried the stolen game password on Tara's other accounts. That is called credential stuffing. Because Tara used exactly the same password on all three, it opened all three. Together they use each site's official recovery steps, change every password, and sign out other devices.
scenes.dialogue: Mum, one leak opened all my accounts?

scenes.label: Three keys
scenes.title: Give every door its own key.
scenes.caption: Your turn. We will practise with familiar words, like Mango and Rocket, with numbers and symbols attached. You can read the words inside each password. Pick an account, then join two tiles without spaces. Give every account a different password and replay the breach. If you copy the full game password, that stolen password opens the other account too. Adding a symbol to your name is still easy to guess. These examples are only for practice. Make real passwords privately with a trusted adult.
scenes.dialogue: Words I know. A different password for every account.

scenes.label: Remember them all
scenes.title: Many keys, one safe place.
scenes.caption: The stolen game password no longer opens Tara's other accounts. The next question is how to remember different passwords. With Mum's help, a password manager can create and save a long, random password for each account. If they do not use one, Mum can keep a written record secure at home. They also turn on two-step verification where available. It adds another check at sign-in.
scenes.dialogue: Different passwords keep one leak from spreading.

scenes.label: A happier ending
scenes.title: Back in the sky garden!
scenes.caption: Tara is back in her sky garden! Her game, school and email accounts each have a different password. Remember: long, hard to guess, private, and different for every account. A password manager can make and safely save real passwords with a trusted adult's help. Never copy a classroom example for a real login. Two-step verification adds another sign-in check. Ask a trusted adult for help if an account is taken over.
scenes.dialogue: Level twenty, and every account has its own password!
